name: IRES-Targeted Translation Modulation
therapeuticGoalDescription: Increase or decrease protein synthesis by regulating mRNA translation without altering RNA abundance.
molecularDefect: Diseases in which cap-independent translation driven by an internal ribosome entry site sustains expression of a pathogenic protein, or in which IRES-driven translation is aberrantly active.
suitableVariantTypes: Not variant-driven. Applies where an IRES element in the target transcript drives cap-independent translation under stress, in cancer, or during viral infection.
rnaTargetRegion: Structured IRES domains, typically domain IV/V of the 5' UTR.
transcriptRequirement: Target transcript containing a validated or predicted internal ribosome entry site.
asoChemistry: RNase H-independent steric-blocking ASOs: PMO, 2'-MOE full-phosphorothioate, LNA/DNA mixmers
designRules: Steric occupancy only - no RNase H recruitment. IRES activity is context-dependent; efficiency varies by cell type and stress conditions; no clinical precedent.
advantages: Targets cap-independent translation active in stress, cancer, and viral infection; structurally well-characterized.
limitations: IRES activity is context-dependent; efficiency varies by cell type and stress conditions; no clinical precedent.
offTargetConsiderations: Must distinguish viral from cellular IRES; off-target effects on other structured RNA elements possible.
clinicalTrialExamples: None identified; preclinical proof-of-concept in HCV IRES and cellular IRES (XIAP, Bcl-2).

evidenceLevel.note: Well-characterized structural biology; preclinical only; no approved therapy.

arbitration.note: IRES domains have conserved secondary structure; ASO binding to domain IV/V disrupts ITAF recruitment.
